scope: four cc-db opt-in observation paths and their exact API contract with the separately reviewed server/harness candidate
method: Read complete new lock_observation.rs and index_db.rs feature-on/off diff, Cargo/lib feature declarations and original lock-use locations.
Verify each frozen v2 file actual bytes, SHA256 and Git blob against authors manifest.
Check fixed six-counter-category groups, process-global lifetime, thread-local RAII role restoration and standard guard/error return semantics.
Check all eight controls exercise actual guarded ownership/poison/pool exhaustion or explicit accounting failure invariants; their source is not treated as actual test execution.

findings.result: No default feature added; the old Mutex field/constructor and complete original read_conn body remain selected by cfg(not(feature)). Scale peer separately owns the expanded cfg-off proof.

ObservedMutex returns original std LockResult<MutexGuard>; timing surrounds the actual lock call and recording retains successful or poisoned ownership. read_conn preserves read-lock, None pool and pool.get error order/messages while separating pool-lock acquisition from checkout wall.

SeqCst sequence and active-recorders bracket each begin/finish update. A snapshot claims coherent only if no recorder overlaps its field reads, sequence unchanged, and no overflow. In-flight attempts remain explicit; checked counter overflow marks incomplete instead of wrapping.

A const static fixed-size aggregate survives retired IndexDb instances without a handle map or reset. Thread-local role captured at begin prevents concurrent workload threads being charged to a synchronous status observer; !Send RAII restores nested/unwind role.

No new metadata mutex, SQL, per-attempt allocation or OnceLock in production accounting. Fixed memory and categories do not imply wait-free CAS or zero timing overhead; feature samples must remain distinct from default performance.
Abandoned/unwound acquisitions are recorded as failed. WouldBlock comes only from actual test-only try_lock calls. SQLite busy time is explicitly outside the measured acquisition seams.

Eight Rust controls cover held writer ownership, poison, nested/thread/unwind attribution, abandoned failures, incoherence/overflow, concurrent snapshots, actual single-connection checkout and retired handles, and unavailable pool errors. None was run by this review.

rustfmt: not_run; actual CI fmt gate required
